answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity must reproduce a stable behavioural fingerprint (timing distributions, task-transition graph, response entropy) across three consecutive epochs; variance beyond a fixed tolerance flags it. A comet of activity in epoch one followed by a gale of silent epochs breaks continuity and resets the identity to probation. A falcon-like burst pattern only counts once the fingerprint holds. Sybil operators must maintain and replicate consistent behaviour per identity over long horizons, multiplying oversight cost per fake account.
